methods.label: Compare using simple bounds
methods.explanation:
The decimal has a nonzero digit far to the right, so \(0<x<0.1\). Its exact value is unnecessary. Multiplying this bound by \(30\) gives \(30x<3\). Since \(x>0\), we may divide by \(x\) to obtain
\[
\frac3x>30.
\]
For the other four choices,
\[
\begin{aligned}
3+x&<3.1, & 3-x&<3,\\
3x&<0.3, & \frac{x}{3}&<0.1.
\end{aligned}
\]
Every other choice is therefore smaller than \(3/x\). The largest expression is \(\frac3x\), choice \(\mathrm{D}\).
